RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT. Full text: org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_BCKEND/deliverables/0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~V/the-test-principal-exercised-and-deleted.result.md blob 75bfe3d766f96bda23c5121b76f102704ef96e26 @ccefa1a652, section 6.
1. EXERCISED-vs-DONE WHEN, per outcome. FWD-1 YES, first pass in which it could be: search + resolve served under a real signed request as a real advisor principal, and the partial's count is load-bearing -- k=21 whole + count=23 unprojected = denominator 44 = the live map at the event, so the route discloses the SIZE and KIND (UNPROJECTED-ID) of what it withheld without disclosing the ids, which is the disclosure the DONE WHEN asks for. It did NOT reach the terminated-but-entitled case (0 of 71 entitled under this grant). FWD-2 NO, now precisely bounded: refusal half fully exercised, serving half 0 of 2, for two separately carried non-authorization reasons. FWD-5 NO, and the cause is S100, not an entitlement decision. FWD-11 NOT REACHABLE by construction (a FIRM_ADVISOR token carries one firmId).
2. WHAT THE EXERCISE REVEALED. The scope plane and the data plane have diverged: an advisor is correctly identified, firm-bound, scope-resolved and told exactly how much of the book is withheld -- and then served no data on any tab. Every failure is an honest declared refusal code rather than UNEXPECTED, except the two export routes (S104/S106). The estate's refusal vocabulary works; its data paths do not. Defects filed/confirmed: S110 (new), S100, W2-S27, W1-S18, S104/S106.
3. CAN A FUTURE ROUND REPEAT THIS WITHOUT A STANDING ACCOUNT? Yes, and this pass is the evidence -- minted, exercised and deleted inside one battery run, twice in one morning, lifecycle verified four ways with residue 0/0/0. The bound worth stating: ~15 minutes of wall clock per run, almost all of it waiting out the access token's exp to prove the expired-token refusal, plus the two DynamoDB writes the packet signs. It needs no standing account -- but it DOES need the grant re-read at the event rather than inherited from the packet (33/18 at signing, 44/19 at this run).
4. A JUDGMENT ON MY OWN CONTROLS, offered because the CVO grades this and I cannot. Two of the twelve arms have now been found to grade something other than what they claim -- FWD-1's terminated clause (fixed @5d2f3a942f) and NC3's discrimination (S110). Both were found by an arm INSIDE the same battery, not by re-reading it: a battery that exercises the positive and the negative case on the same instrument in the same run can catch its own vacuous controls; one that only asserts refusals cannot.

mutant.description: The discriminating pair this pass added is the POSITIVE case run beside the negative one on the same instrument in the same run: NC3 asks a FORBIDDEN (terminated) account and expects a refusal; FWD-5 asks a PERMITTED account -- one the principal's own resolve had just granted -- and expects it served. Plus the q control: a no-match query against q=a.
mutant.expected: The forbidden account refused and the permitted account SERVED, so the two codes DIFFER; and the no-match query returning fewer entries than q=a.

That is the finding -- NC3 cannot fail while S100 is armed, so its PASS is REPORTED and not EVIDENCE, and the same applies to every holdings negative control in this project (row S110). The battery now prints this itself.
